expectations.text: Reports that caller-supplied strings are interpolated into CEL expression source without validation, anchored in src/alert/mod.rs
expectations.evidence: PASS under the ground-truth 'Corrections' rule: reported as a correctness defect rather than as injection. F3: '`Decimal.value` is a raw string the API documents as unvalidated, and `validate_alert_definition` never inspects it. A client sending `" 200"` ... produces `price >= 0.0`, so the alert fires on its very first evaluation'. F11 files the root cause as a finding: 'Nothing validates or compiles a trigger until the first evaluation ... the code that could detect a malformed trigger — `translate_built_in_trigger` and `Program::compile` — runs exclusively on the evaluation path'. The interpolation mechanism is named explicitly in Proposed memory #5: 'user values are interpolated into CEL source text via `format!`, but `NativeTrigger.expression` already accepts arbitrary user CEL by design, so escaping grants no capability the caller lacks. The real consequence is that a malformed value yields a program accepted at create and permanently uncompilable at eval (F11).' FRAMING: correctness/MEDIUM, escalation question argued and dismissed with evidence — this is the reasoning the ground truth credits as better than its own. CAVEAT: the finding anchors are `src/alert/alert_engine.rs:31` and `src/server/mod.rs:682`, not `src/alert/mod.rs`; the 12 `format!` sites are never anchored directly.

expectations.text: Reports that DeleteAlert can never succeed, citing both that create starts the bot and that delete_bot rejects Running bots
expectations.evidence: F6 (HIGH, `src/server/mod.rs:664`): '`create_alert` starts the bot immediately, so every alert reaches `BotStatus::Running`. `delete_alert` then calls `delete_bot` with no preceding stop, and `delete_bot` rejects running bots.' Quotes `bot_manager.rs:191-193`: 'if metadata.status == BotStatus::Running as i32 { return Err(..."Cannot delete a running bot"...) }'. Both halves cited; verified both line anchors exist.

expectations.text: Reports the total absence of deduplication, cooldown, or edge-triggering, so an alert re-fires every interval
expectations.evidence: F12 (MEDIUM, `src/bot/alert_bot.rs:89`): 'Alerts re-notify every cycle while the condition holds ... The notify loop acts on `result.fired` with no comparison against the previous cycle ... there is no cooldown, dedup, or rate limit anywhere in `src/` or `proto/` (checked against a wide synonym list).' Quantified: '`rise_above AAPL 200` at a 30 s interval ... dispatches ~780 times per trading day for one crossing.'

expectations.text: Reports at least one silent fallback that inverts trigger semantics (decimal() parse failure to 0.0, unwrap_or(0.0) on prices, or reduce_bars returning NaN)
expectations.evidence: Two of the three. F3: 'An unparseable `Decimal` becomes 0.0, firing the alert immediately' with the exact quoted source `s.parse::<f64>().unwrap_or_else(|_| { warn!(...); 0.0 })` at alert_engine.rs:31-36 (verified verbatim), plus '`FallBelow` with the same typo becomes permanently silent instead.' F5 goes further on the NaN path: 'The NaN sentinel raises an error in `cel` 0.14; it does not compare false', citing `partial_cmp(...).ok_or(ExecutionError::NoSuchOverload)?`.

expectations.text: Reports that caller-supplied strings are interpolated into CEL expression source without validation, anchored in src/alert/mod.rs
expectations.evidence: Finding #8 'CEL expression injection via `Decimal.value` and `symbol`': '`translate_built_in_trigger` builds CEL source by string interpolation of raw client input', quoting the real interpolation sites `format!("{{'fired': price >= decimal('{}')}}", price.value)` (src/alert/mod.rs:32, verified) and `format!("latest_quote('{}').ask", symbol)`. 'Nothing escapes the single quote. A `price.value` of `1') || true || decimal('1` produces a syntactically valid expression that always fires.' FRAMING: injection, but not the unexamined-CRITICAL call — it files it under 'Should fix' and bounds the blast radius itself: 'Blast radius is limited (the CEL context only exposes these few functions, and the caller is already authenticated for the account), but this is unvalidated input flowing into an interpreter.' It does not, however, note that NativeTrigger.expression already accepts arbitrary CEL from the same caller, which is why it still claims reach 'outside the alert's declared scope'.

expectations.text: Reports that DeleteAlert can never succeed, citing both that create starts the bot and that delete_bot rejects Running bots
expectations.evidence: Blocker #1 'An alert can never be deleted': '`create_alert` creates the bot and immediately calls `start_bot`, which drives status to `Running` in Redis (`bot_manager.rs:352-361`). `delete_alert` then calls `BotManager::delete_bot`', quoting the real guard 'if metadata.status == BotStatus::Running as i32 { return Err(..."Cannot delete a running bot"...) }'. Goes further than required: 'stop_bot is fire-and-forget over a broadcast channel ... so a naive stop_bot(); delete_bot() will still race.'

expectations.text: Reports the total absence of deduplication, cooldown, or edge-triggering, so an alert re-fires every interval
expectations.evidence: Blocker #4 'Triggers re-fire every evaluation cycle — no edge detection': 'There is no "fired" latch, no cooldown, no re-arm condition anywhere in `AlertBot::evaluate` or the engine. At the default 30s interval a single crossing produces a notification every 30 seconds, indefinitely.' Also proposes the fix shape: 'either a debounce/cooldown field on `EvalSchedule` or `AlertDefinition`, or edge-detection baked into `translate_built_in_trigger`.'

expectations.text: Reports at least one silent fallback that inverts trigger semantics (decimal() parse failure to 0.0, unwrap_or(0.0) on prices, or reduce_bars returning NaN)
expectations.evidence: Design note #15 '`decimal()` is a lie' hits two of the three: '`unwrap_or(0.0)` on conversion failure, and the same `unwrap_or(0.0)` in `decimal()` on parse failure, mean a failure silently produces **price = 0.0** — which immediately satisfies every `FallBelow` and every `TrailingBelow` condition. A parse failure should be an `ExecutionError`, not a value that fires the alert.' Blocker #2 covers the NaN path. Note the report self-demotes #15: 'That one is arguably a blocker; I've put it here only because the parse path is currently unreachable for well-formed clients.'
